s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral facial weakness with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Slight slant of mouth corners towards left
Disappearance of nasolabial fold in right face
key_facts: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI
No hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images
No vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis on MRTA
Significantly decreased amplitude of right facial nerve compound muscular action potential on ENoG
Presence of insertional activity in right facial muscles with greatly reduced voluntary activity on EMG

salient_findings: Slight slant of mouth corners towards left
Disappearance of nasolabial fold in right face
key_facts: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

differentials: Epidermoid cyst of the posterior fossa

shortlist.label: Pontine glioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive unilateral facial weakness with associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Brainstem glioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI and progressive neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial weakness and associated neurological symptoms such as hearing loss and diplopia

shortlist.label: Stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of neurological symptoms including weakness and diplopia

raw.rationale: The lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI, along with the hypo-intense signal in T1-weighted images and moderate-intense signal in T2-weighted images, is consistent with a brainstem glioma. The patient's symptoms, including facial muscle weakness and cranial nerve deficits, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pontine glioma
rejected.why: While similar, pontine glioma is a more specific type of brainstem glioma, and the provided information does not specifically indicate the tumor is limited to the pons.

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The lesion's location in the brainstem and the patient's symptoms are not typical for a facial nerve schwannoma, which usually presents with a more localized effect on the facial nerve.

rejected.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a rash and pain in the ear, along with facial weakness, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Stroke
rejected.why: The absence of hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images on MRI and the lack of vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis on MRTA make an acute stroke less likely.

rejected.label: Stroke
rejected.why: The gradual progression of symptoms over 7 months is not typical for a stroke, which usually has a more abrupt onset.
